Definition: from G2808; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively:--key.
KeyPassages: Matthew 16:19; Luke 11:52; Revelation 1:18; Revelation 3:7; Revelation 9:1; Revelation 20:1
BiblicalUsage: Kleis is a key, the thing that shuts and opens. Matthew 16:19 gives Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, Luke 11:52 rebukes the lawyers who have taken away the key of knowledge, Revelation 1:18 has the risen Christ holding the keys of hell and of death, Revelation 3:7 gives the key of David to Him that openeth and no man shutteth, and Revelation 9:1 and Revelation 20:1 give the key of the bottomless pit to the angel who binds the dragon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the keys all belong to one hand in the end: Peter holds them by gift, the lawyers lose them by theft, and Christ holds the keys of hell and of death because He died and lives again. I hold that the key of David is the key of the whole Bible, that the door Christ opens no man shuts.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Simon Peter; John the Apostle
